episode_title: Fastest Four: Stocks Rose in 21 of 25 Midterm Novembers. Will 2026 Follow?

real_qa.q: What percentage of midterm election Novembers have seen stock market gains historically?
real_qa.r: According to Morningstar research studying a century of market performance, stocks have risen in the month of November in 21 of the past 25 midterm election years, which equals 84% of the time. Morningstar strategist Dan Lefkowitz concluded that the post-election pop is real, regardless of election results.

real_qa.q: How much did the S&P 500 earnings growth track in 2026 third quarter?
real_qa.r: S&P 500 earnings growth in 2026 third quarter is tracking near 30%, with 179 of the S&P 500 companies reporting earnings that week. This earnings growth has been enormous, driven not just by mega tech companies but also by companies outside the AI trade expected to deliver strong profit growth of potentially 20%.

real_qa.q: What was the stock market performance through August in a midterm election year like 2026?
real_qa.r: BlackRock reports that the stock market was up 13.1% through August, which is the sixth strongest start to a midterm year since 1926. This strong performance early in the year may make it more difficult to expect as much post-election optimism.

real_qa.q: Which non-tech sectors are projected to generate double-digit earnings gains according to LPL Research?
real_qa.r: According to LPL Research, six of the ten non-tech sectors are projected to generate double-digit earnings gains. LPL Research's base case is that the outlook for corporate profits remains encouraging, and the research team still expects double-digit S&P 500 earnings growth in 2027.
